purpose: A bounded method for acquiring medical-alert customers honestly: mapping the three-party buyer triangle of wearer, adult-child payer and professional referrer, building home-care, senior-centre and discharge-planner referral channels inside the referral-inducement boundary, designing a device-plus-monitoring offer whose total cost and exit terms are disclosed before any ask, holding vulnerable-consumer and no-fear-selling constraints as hard stops rather than preferences, substantiating every reliability claim instead of asserting it, positioning honestly against national brands and consumer-electronics alternatives, deciding when to decline a sale outright, and gating a signed, assented, fully disclosed account into installation.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the business sells emergency-signaling equipment plus a monitoring subscription; it is not a clinical service and employs no licensed clinician in the selling role
the buying population is older adults and their families, treated throughout as a vulnerable-consumer class rather than as ordinary retail buyers
monitoring capacity is bought wholesale from a monitoring centre and resold as a subscription, so account economics are governed by the operator's own quoted costs, not by any industry-wide figure

licensing, telemarketing, home-solicitation and referral-compensation obligations differ by jurisdiction and change; every rule named here is an obligation class the operator must verify currently in their own jurisdiction

reliability characteristics (battery endurance, radio range, fall-detection sensitivity, monitoring-centre answer performance) are properties of specific equipment and a specific monitoring contract, verified per deployment rather than assumed from a brochure
exclusions: device-type selection, home range and connectivity assessment, mounting, monitoring-centre integration, emergency-contact-tree configuration, the mandatory end-to-end signal test and wearer training — that is the device setup and testing knowledge base this one hands off to

running the live subscription: periodic test-call cadence, battery and device-health monitoring, address and contact currency, service recovery after a missed signal, and dignified cancellation when a wearer moves to higher care or dies — that is the monitoring, retention and caregiver-relations knowledge base

post-installation referral loops harvested from well-served families and their caregivers, which belong to the retention knowledge base; this knowledge base covers only pre-sale professional-channel building and its acquisition economics
any clinical judgment: fall-risk assessment, capacity determination, medication questions, whether an older adult can safely live alone, or whether a device is medically indicated
personalized financial, legal, tax or insurance advice, including whether a plan, benefit programme or long-term-care policy will reimburse a monitoring subscription

asserting specific prices, monitoring wholesale rates, commissions, response times, market sizes or churn percentages as fact; all money and performance content is expressed as a mechanism or a qualitative band the operator instantiates from their own quotes and tests
installation labour scheduling, technician routing and field service management

glossary.definition: The equipment class this business sells: a wearable or fixed help button that, when pressed or triggered, opens a voice or data path to a monitoring centre which then works a written contact procedure. It is signaling equipment, not a diagnostic or therapeutic device, and it does nothing on its own unless the monitoring subscription behind it is live.

The contracted operation that receives alarm signals, speaks to the wearer, and dispatches emergency services or contacts the family per the account's instructions. The operator resells its capacity; its contractual answer-performance commitments, staffing and redundancy are the substance behind any service claim made to a customer.

A sensor-and-algorithm feature that attempts to recognise a fall and raise an alarm without a button press. It is a probabilistic feature with both missed events and false alarms, and its capability class must be described to families in exactly those terms rather than as a guarantee that a fall will be caught.

The three-party structure of nearly every medical-alert sale: the older adult who wears the device and must accept it, the adult child or spouse who usually pays and often initiates, and the care professional whose recommendation created the opening. Each has different fears, different information and different veto power.

The older adult's own, separately obtained agreement to wear the device, distinct from the payer's decision to buy it. Assent is the difference between an account that stays live and a pendant that sits in a drawer, and its absence is a decline condition rather than an objection to overcome.

The hospital or skilled-nursing staff member (often a nurse or social worker) who arranges what happens when a patient goes home. They typically operate under vendor-neutrality expectations, hand out lists rather than recommendations, and are one of the highest-intent referral sources precisely because they meet families at the transition moment.

The obligation class governing what may be given to someone who sends business, especially when the source touches healthcare. Cash per referral, gifts of value and revenue splits with clinically-adjacent sources sit in a restricted zone whose specifics vary by jurisdiction and source type and must be verified currently before any arrangement is made.

The single figure a family should hear before being asked to decide: every one-time charge plus every recurring charge for the first twelve months plus any optional feature they have said yes to, plus shipping and applicable tax. It is the operator's own arithmetic on their own price sheet, and its function is to make hidden-fee surprise structurally impossible.

The short written note created when this business refuses a sale it could have made — no viable connectivity, no wearer assent, a need better served by a higher level of care, or a household that cannot afford the subscription without hardship. It names the disqualifying condition, what was offered instead, and who was told.

The way a monitoring account repays what it cost to win: the one-time margin on equipment and activation plus the accumulated monthly gross margin on the subscription, set against the fully-loaded cost of acquiring and installing that account. The operator computes it from their own quoted equipment cost, wholesale monitoring rate and channel spend; no industry figure substitutes for that arithmetic.

nodes.definition: Write down, before any family conversation happens, exactly what this business sells, what it refuses to do, and the sentence used out loud when a request crosses that line. A medical-alert business sells emergency-signaling equipment plus a monitoring subscription: a wearable or fixed button that opens a path to a monitoring centre, which then works a written contact procedure. It does not assess whether an older adult is safe living alone, does not judge fall risk, does not diagnose, does not recommend or discourage a level of care, and does not promise a medical outcome. The charter names the equipment and service classes actually carried, the neutral destinations an out-of-scope question is sent to — the person's own clinician, the hospital's discharge team, a licensed social worker or geriatric care manager, the public ageing-services agency class — and the standing sentence that the decision to have a device, and to wear it, belongs to the older adult. It exists because scope collapses precisely in the moment a frightened daughter asks whether her mother should still be living alone: a question the person selling the pendant is unqualified to answer and commercially motivated to answer wrongly.

included: the equipment-plus-monitoring definition of what is being sold
the explicit refusal list covering clinical, capacity, legal and benefit-eligibility questions
named neutral referral destinations and the standing decision-ownership sentence
excluded: which device model suits a given home, which is assessed and configured in the device setup and testing knowledge base
in-service commitments to the live account, which belong to the monitoring and retention knowledge base
any determination of medical need or cognitive capacity, which is never this business's call

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a recorded conversation shows a staff member answering a clinical or capacity question, or a new product class is carried that the charter does not describe

pros.claim: A written refusal list converts the hardest live moments into a rehearsed sentence instead of an improvisation made under a family's emotional pressure
pros.example: a son asking whether his father's dizziness means he needs a device or a doctor gets the referral sentence to the prescribing clinician, not a sales opinion dressed as concern

pros.claim: Stating plainly that this is signaling equipment rather than medical care raises trust with exactly the families who have been called by four other companies that month
pros.example: opening a senior-centre talk by saying the device does not prevent a fall and does not replace a doctor, then explaining what it actually does when a fall happens

cons.claim: A charter drawn too narrowly makes the operator refuse legitimate product education, pushing the family back toward whichever advertiser will say anything
cons.example: declining to explain in general terms how fall detection works because the charter conflated product explanation with clinical advice

cons.claim: A charter that lives only in a binder changes nothing unless the website copy, call scripts and event language are rewritten to match it
cons.example: a homepage headline promising peace of mind and safety while the charter says the product signals for help and nothing more

failure_modes: scope that exists only in the owner's head and quietly widens whenever a large or emotional sale pushes on it
answering a medical or capacity question conversationally because saying it is outside our scope feels unhelpful while a family is crying
marketing language that implies clinical authority, hospital endorsement or a guaranteed outcome
acceptance_tests: the charter names the equipment and monitoring classes carried, at least four out-of-scope question types, and a named neutral destination for each
the refusal sentence and the decision-ownership sentence appear verbatim in the call script, the website copy and the community-talk outline
revisit_triggers: a new product class is added, such as mobile GPS units or a caregiver mobile application
a staff member reports being asked an out-of-scope question the charter does not cover
marketing copy is rewritten by anyone outside the business

nodes.definition: Treat every prospect as a member of a vulnerable-consumer class and encode the resulting limits as hard stops with enforcement, not as values on a wall. The rules that matter in this business are specific: no same-visit pressure close when the older adult is alone and no family member has been consulted; no contract signed by a person who cannot restate in their own words what they are buying and what it costs monthly; no unsolicited in-home visit or call without a request or a documented referral, with telemarketing, do-not-call and home-solicitation cooling-off obligations treated as an obligation class to verify currently in the operator's jurisdiction; no payment method that cannot be stopped by the customer; no bundling of a signature for something else with a monitoring agreement; and an explicit right for any family member to slow the process down. Enforcement means each stop has a mechanism — a mandatory second-contact step, a teach-back question, a script line the salesperson cannot skip, a card the customer keeps with the cancellation phone number. Without mechanisms the rules survive only until the first month the sales numbers are short.

included: the enumerated hard stops for selling to older adults and their enforcement mechanisms
teach-back confirmation of what is bought and what it costs each month
the obligation classes for solicitation, cooling-off and payment-method reversibility, each flagged for jurisdictional verification
excluded: determining cognitive capacity or competence, which is a clinical and legal judgment this business never makes
post-sale service conduct and cancellation handling during the live subscription, which belong to the retention knowledge base
drafting the contract's legal language, which is counsel's work

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint, chargeback or family dispute reveals a stop that was skipped, or the jurisdiction changes a solicitation or automatic-renewal obligation

pros.claim: Hard stops with mechanisms hold under quota pressure, which is exactly when soft values fail
pros.example: a mandatory teach-back question that stops a signature when the prospect cannot say what the monthly charge is, even though the salesperson is behind for the month

pros.claim: A slow, family-inclusive process produces accounts that survive, because the person paying and the person wearing both understood what they agreed to
pros.example: a second conversation with the daughter on speakerphone that surfaces an existing device in the house before a duplicate subscription is sold

cons.claim: Deliberate friction loses genuinely wanted sales to faster, less scrupulous competitors who will close on the first visit
cons.example: a family that wanted the device that day buys from a national advertiser overnight because this business insisted on a second conversation

cons.claim: Rules written as a compliance checklist can be performed hollowly, producing a signed acknowledgement page with no actual understanding behind it
cons.example: reading the disclosure aloud at speed to a hard-of-hearing prospect and collecting the initials

failure_modes: treating the vulnerable-consumer rules as a training slide rather than as blocking steps in the sales workflow
letting a family member's urgency override the wearer's own pace because the family member is the one paying
using autopay enrolment on a payment instrument the customer cannot easily stop
acceptance_tests: each hard stop names the mechanism that enforces it and the artifact that proves it happened for a given account
a randomly sampled recent sale shows the teach-back answer recorded and a cancellation-contact card issued to the customer
revisit_triggers: a complaint alleging pressure, confusion about charges, or an unwanted subscription
a change in the jurisdiction's solicitation, cooling-off or automatic-renewal obligation class
a new sales channel or a new salesperson joins the business

nodes.definition: Establish that no reliability claim reaches a customer's ears until a named source and a stated test condition exist behind it. Four claim classes carry nearly all the risk in this business: battery endurance, radio or cellular range, fall-detection capability, and how quickly and reliably a signal is answered. Each needs a different substantiation source — the manufacturer's published specification with its measurement conditions for battery and range, the monitoring centre's contractual performance commitment and its own reporting for answer performance, and the manufacturer's own capability description plus the operator's site test for fall detection. The rule has three parts: name the source, repeat the condition attached to it, and downgrade the wording when neither exists. A specification measured in ideal conditions becomes 'the manufacturer specifies this under their stated test conditions; your house will be measured at installation', not 'it reaches everywhere in your home'. Advertising-substantiation duties are an obligation class to verify currently in the operator's jurisdiction, but the operating rule is stricter and simpler: if the operator cannot say where a number came from, the number is not said at all.

included: the four high-risk claim classes and the substantiation source required for each
the requirement to repeat the measurement condition alongside any specification figure
the downgrade wording used when substantiation is absent, and the deferral to installation-time verification
excluded: performing the actual range, signal and end-to-end tests at the home, which is the device setup and testing knowledge base's mandatory protocol
ongoing device-health and battery monitoring on live accounts, which belongs to the retention knowledge base
engineering evaluation or bench testing of equipment beyond what the operator can verify in a real home

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a catalogue model or firmware revision changes, the monitoring contract's performance terms change, or a claim is challenged by a customer or referrer

pros.claim: Sourced claims survive the moment a family checks them, and unsourced ones become the reason a family cancels and tells their referrer why
pros.example: quoting the manufacturer's battery figure with its standby-condition caveat, then showing the family where it is printed, rather than rounding it up in conversation

pros.claim: Deferring the definitive answer to the installation test turns an unprovable sales claim into a scheduled, verifiable event the customer watches happen
pros.example: telling a customer that whether the pendant reaches the back garden will be measured and written down at installation instead of promising coverage

cons.claim: Careful, conditioned claims sound weaker beside a competitor's flat superlative, and some buyers read precision as hedging
cons.example: a family choosing an advertiser promising nationwide coverage over an operator who explained that coverage depends on the carrier signal at that address

cons.claim: Maintaining sourced claim sheets across several models and a monitoring contract is real recurring administrative work that decays when a model changes
cons.example: a discontinued pendant's superseded battery specification still circulating in a printed comparison sheet

failure_modes: repeating a marketing brochure's headline figure as if it were a measured guarantee for this customer's home
describing fall detection as if every fall is caught, omitting both missed events and false alarms
quoting an answer-time expectation the monitoring contract does not actually commit to
acceptance_tests: every reliability figure used in any customer-facing material traces to a named source document with its measurement condition recorded beside it
the fall-detection description in use states both the missed-event and the false-alarm possibility in plain language
revisit_triggers: a device model, firmware or accessory in the catalogue changes
the monitoring centre contract or its performance reporting changes
a customer or referrer disputes a claim made during a sale

nodes.definition: Draw and police the line between informing a family about a real risk and frightening an older adult into a purchase. The distinction is testable rather than aesthetic: informing describes what the product does when something happens and leaves the decision with the listener; frightening describes what will happen to the listener if they do not buy, uses an unfalsifiable personal prediction, or manufactures urgency. In this business the banned patterns are specific — telling a person living alone that they will die on the floor, telling an adult child they will find their parent too late, asserting that the device will save a life, presenting a statistic about falls without its source or population, inventing a deadline on a price, and describing a competitor's absence of a feature as danger. Each banned pattern needs a written honest replacement, because salespeople under pressure reach for whatever sentence is available. The replacement for the death image is a plain description of what happens when the button is pressed and how long help typically takes to arrive in that area; the replacement for manufactured urgency is the truthful statement that the offer is not going anywhere.

included: the testable informing-versus-frightening distinction
the enumerated banned claim and imagery patterns with their honest replacement wording
the ban on manufactured deadlines and unsourced fall statistics
excluded: product capability explanation, which belongs to competitive positioning and the substantiation rule
the reassurance language used with families of live accounts after an incident, which belongs to the retention knowledge base
refusing to discuss risk at all, which leaves the family less informed than they were

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint about pressure or fear, a new advertising campaign draft, or a review of sales recordings finding a banned pattern in live use

pros.claim: A written banned-and-replacement list gives a salesperson something honest to say in the exact second the fear line would otherwise be crossed
pros.example: replacing the image of lying on the floor for two days with a factual walkthrough of the pressed-button sequence and who gets called in what order

pros.claim: Refusing fear appeals protects the referral channels, because professionals stop referring the moment a client reports being frightened into buying
pros.example: a senior-centre director continuing to host talks after checking with attendees that nobody felt pressured

cons.claim: Avoiding fear entirely can understate a genuine risk and leave a family without the information they needed to make a decision
cons.example: never mentioning that an unwitnessed fall is the specific scenario the product addresses, leaving a family unclear what it is for

cons.claim: The boundary is judgment-laden at the margins, so two honest salespeople will disagree about the same sentence
cons.example: arguing over whether mentioning a neighbour's recent long lie is context or emotional leverage

failure_modes: using a real customer's emergency story as a sales instrument without consent and without its ordinary outcome
quoting a fall statistic with no source, population or date attached to it
inventing a price deadline or a device-availability shortage to force a same-day decision
acceptance_tests: each banned pattern in the list has a written honest replacement sentence, and both appear in the training material
a review of recent recorded or observed sales conversations finds no unfalsifiable personal prediction and no manufactured deadline
revisit_triggers: a customer or family member reports feeling frightened into buying
a new campaign, script or advertisement is drafted
a competitor's fear-based campaign creates pressure to answer it in kind

nodes.definition: For each opportunity, identify explicitly who wears the device, who pays for it, who influences the decision, and who holds legal authority — because in this business those are rarely the same person and the sale fails at whichever corner was assumed. The wearer is the older adult whose cooperation determines whether the device is ever on their body. The payer is usually an adult child or a spouse, often living elsewhere, who initiates contact and asks the price questions. The influencer is frequently a professional — a home-care aide, a discharge planner, a therapist — whose recommendation opened the door and whose continued trust depends on how this sale is conducted. Authority is separate again: a power of attorney or guardian may be the only person who can lawfully sign, which is an obligation class to verify currently rather than a matter this business decides. Mapping the triangle means writing down, per opportunity, each named person, their role, their stated fear, what they must hear, and who has veto power, so that the conversation is designed for the right listener instead of whoever answered the telephone.

included: per-opportunity identification of wearer, payer, influencer and signing authority with names and roles
each party's stated fear and the information each specifically needs
identification of who holds veto power over the decision
excluded: the emergency-contact tree used by the monitoring centre, which is configured in the device setup knowledge base
ongoing family communication on a live account, which belongs to the caregiver-relations knowledge base
determining whether a power of attorney is valid, which is a legal question referred out

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an opportunity is lost or an installed account goes unused in a way traced back to a party whose role was never mapped

pros.claim: Naming the roles up front prevents the classic failure of selling only to the payer and installing a device the wearer never agreed to
pros.example: discovering during mapping that the mother has already refused a pendant twice, which changes the entire conversation before any pricing is discussed

pros.claim: Knowing who referred the opportunity lets the operator honour the professional relationship that produced it
pros.example: learning the occupational therapist suggested the call, and keeping the therapist's guidance in view rather than upselling past it

cons.claim: Role mapping adds a discovery step that can feel intrusive to a family in the first minutes of a stressful call
cons.example: asking who has power of attorney before the daughter has finished explaining what happened to her father last week

cons.claim: Roles shift mid-process, so a map made once and never revisited produces a confident but wrong conversation plan
cons.example: a second sibling entering the decision late with different priorities and effective veto power

failure_modes: treating the person who telephoned as the decision-maker without ever speaking to the person who will wear the device
missing that the household already has a device or a service under a different family member's name
ignoring an absent sibling who will fund or block the purchase
acceptance_tests: the opportunity record names each party with role, contact, stated concern and veto status before any price is quoted
the wearer has been spoken with directly, or a documented reason exists why that has not yet happened
revisit_triggers: a new family member joins the conversation or the paying party changes
the wearer's living situation changes during the sales process
the referring professional's involvement ends or transfers

nodes.definition: Obtain the older adult's own agreement to wear the device, separately from the payer's decision to buy it, and treat its absence as a reason to decline rather than an objection to overcome. Refusal in this population is usually rational and specific: the pendant is a public admission of frailty, it is uncomfortable or ugly, it looks like the first step toward being moved out of the house, or the person does not believe they need it. Assent work means hearing which of those it is and answering the actual objection — showing the wristband and clip alternatives for the person who hates a necklace, being honest with the person who fears it signals decline that the device exists so they can stay home longer, and letting the person who genuinely does not want it say no without the family steamrolling them. Assent is also the strongest predictor available at the point of sale of whether the account survives, because a device that lives in a drawer produces a cancellation and a family that feels sold to. It is recorded in the wearer's own words, not as a checkbox the payer ticks on their behalf.

included: separately obtained agreement from the person who will wear the device, recorded in their own words
the catalogue of common refusal reasons and the honest response to each
treating persistent refusal as a decline condition rather than an objection to defeat
excluded: wearing-habit coaching and training at installation, which belongs to the device setup knowledge base
re-engaging a wearer who has stopped wearing a live device, which belongs to the retention knowledge base
any assessment of decision-making capacity, which is referred out

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: early cancellations or unworn devices cluster among accounts where assent was recorded second-hand rather than in the wearer's own words

pros.claim: Assent obtained before the sale is the single cheapest defence against an account that cancels within its first months
pros.example: a wearer choosing a wristband style during the sales conversation and saying plainly she will keep it on in the shower

pros.claim: Respecting a refusal preserves the family relationship and often produces the sale later on the wearer's own terms
pros.example: leaving a written summary and no contract after a father declines, and being called back by him after a neighbour's fall

cons.claim: Insisting on the wearer's assent will lose sales the paying adult child is ready to close immediately
cons.example: a daughter who wants the device installed before she flies home on Sunday, when her mother has not agreed to wear anything

cons.claim: Assent can be shallow — agreement given to end an uncomfortable family conversation rather than genuine acceptance
cons.example: a wearer agreeing while her son is present and quietly saying afterward she has no intention of wearing it

failure_modes: accepting the payer's assurance that the wearer is fine with it instead of asking the wearer
arguing a reluctant older adult into agreement in front of their family, which produces compliance rather than assent
skipping the wearing-style conversation so the only option offered is the one the person has already refused
acceptance_tests: the record contains the wearer's own words about wanting the device and the wearing style they chose
where assent was not obtained, a decline-to-sell record exists rather than a booked installation
revisit_triggers: the wearer expresses second thoughts at any point before installation
a family member reports the wearer was pressured
the chosen wearing style proves unworkable for the wearer's hands or skin

nodes.definition: Understand what the paying adult child is actually buying, because it is rarely the equipment. The long-distance caregiver is buying relief from a specific dread and from guilt about distance, and that motive predictably distorts the transaction in three directions: overbuying features that do not fit the parent's life, wanting a promise the operator cannot honestly make, and pushing past the parent's reluctance because the purchase resolves the child's anxiety rather than the parent's problem. Handling this well means naming the fear out loud, stating what the product does and does not change, sizing the purchase to the parent's actual routine rather than the child's imagination, and being explicit that a monitoring subscription is a signaling service and not supervision. It also means recognising the household with real financial strain, where a monthly subscription competes with medication or heating, and saying so rather than selling the largest package available. The payer is a legitimate customer with legitimate fears; the discipline is refusing to monetise the guilt.

included: the payer's real motives and the three distortions they create in the transaction
sizing the purchase to the wearer's routine instead of the payer's anxiety
recognising household financial strain and adjusting or declining accordingly
excluded: ongoing caregiver communication, reporting and reassurance on live accounts, which belong to the caregiver-relations knowledge base
family conflict mediation and estate or authority disputes, which are referred out
advising on how the family should fund the purchase, which is personalized financial advice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a pattern of returned accessories, unused optional features or early downgrades traced to configurations chosen by the payer rather than the wearer's routine

pros.claim: Naming the guilt explicitly defuses the pressure to oversell, because the payer stops asking for a promise once the real fear is on the table
pros.example: telling a daughter directly that no device removes the risk of her mother being alone, and then describing precisely what it does do

pros.claim: Sizing to the parent's actual routine produces a used device and a stable account rather than an expensive one that annoys the wearer
pros.example: declining to add a mobile GPS unit for a woman who leaves the house only with her son driving

cons.claim: Declining the upsell the payer is actively requesting costs immediate revenue and can read as unhelpfulness
cons.example: refusing to sell a second pendant and a lockbox the family asked for because the layout does not need them

cons.claim: Discussing money strain is intrusive and can embarrass a family that will then buy nothing at all
cons.example: raising affordability with a proud parent present, who ends the conversation to avoid the subject

failure_modes: selling the largest package because the anxious payer will agree to anything in the first week after an incident
implying the monitoring service watches over the parent continuously rather than responding to signals
letting the payer's urgency override the wearer's pace and the second-conversation rule
acceptance_tests: the recommended configuration is justified in writing by the wearer's actual routine, not by the payer's requested feature list
the payer has been told in plain words what the service does not do, and that statement appears in the written packet
revisit_triggers: the payer requests features that the wearer's routine does not support
the household's financial situation is disclosed as strained
the paying party changes during the sales process

nodes.definition: Recognise that this product is almost never bought on a calm Tuesday; it is bought inside a narrow window after a specific event, and design the business to be findable in those windows without exploiting them. The recurring triggers are a fall with or without injury, a hospital or rehabilitation discharge back to home, an emergency-department visit, a new diagnosis or medication change that affects balance, the death or hospitalisation of a spouse who had been the informal safety net, an adult child's visit that reveals decline, and a move to a smaller home or in with family. Each window has its own legitimate approach and its own abuse: the discharge window is served by being on a neutral resource list, not by contacting a patient whose information was passed without consent; the post-fall window is served by a referring professional handing over the operator's card, not by cold-calling recent incident addresses. The operational content is a written map of triggers to legitimate presence, plus the deliberate decision to build pre-crisis awareness so families already know the name when the window opens.

included: the enumerated care-transition triggers that create purchase windows
the legitimate presence mechanism for each window and the abuse it must avoid
the pre-crisis awareness strategy that removes dependence on crisis pressure
excluded: any use of patient information obtained without the individual's consent, which is prohibited outright
clinical assessment of what a trigger event means for the person's care needs
post-installation follow-up scheduling, which belongs to the retention knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: lead-source analysis shows which trigger windows actually produce retained accounts, or a referral institution changes how transitions are handled

pros.claim: Knowing the windows lets a small operator concentrate limited channel effort where intent is real instead of advertising to everyone
pros.example: prioritising relationships with the rehabilitation discharge team over generic newspaper advertising

pros.claim: Pre-crisis awareness converts a crisis into a phone call to a known name, which removes the pressure that produces regretted purchases
pros.example: a family calling the operator whose senior-centre talk they attended a year earlier, on the day the discharge date is set

cons.claim: Trigger-window targeting sits close to the ethical line and can slide into crisis exploitation without an explicit prohibition
cons.example: buying a list of recent emergency-service call addresses and mailing the households

cons.claim: Windows are short and unpredictable, so a business built solely on them has volatile, hard-to-forecast demand
cons.example: a month with almost no discharge referrals following a quiet period at the local rehabilitation unit

failure_modes: obtaining or acting on patient information that was never consented to be shared
arriving during the window with a same-day-only price to capitalise on the family's distress
building the whole pipeline on one hospital relationship that ends when a single staff member leaves
acceptance_tests: each listed trigger has a documented legitimate presence mechanism and a named prohibited practice
no lead in the pipeline originates from patient information obtained without consent, verifiable from the lead-source field
revisit_triggers: a referral source's discharge or transition process changes
a competitor begins crisis-window practices that create pressure to match them
lead-source review shows dependence on a single trigger or a single institution

nodes.definition: Build a written inventory of every local party who meets older adults at the moment this product becomes relevant, and record for each what they can actually do, what they are constrained from doing, and what they need from a vendor. The landscape includes home-care and home-health agencies, hospital and skilled-nursing discharge planners, physical and occupational therapists, the public ageing-services agency class and its information-and-referral function, senior centres and meal programmes, faith communities and their visitation volunteers, elder-law attorneys and geriatric care managers, independent-living community managers, pharmacists, and locksmiths and handymen who work in older adults' homes. Each entry needs four fields: what the source sees that signals need, what form their help can take under their own rules, what they need in return that is permissible, and how volatile the relationship is if a single individual leaves. The map exists because untargeted channel effort is the largest waste in a small operator's week, and because sources differ enormously in what they are permitted to do — a discharge planner constrained to neutral lists and a senior-centre director free to invite a speaker require entirely different approaches.

included: the inventory of local professional and community referral sources with their constraints
what each source sees, what help they can give, and what they need in return
the fragility assessment of each relationship's dependence on individuals
excluded: referral loops from satisfied families and their caregivers after installation, which belong to the retention knowledge base
paying or rewarding sources, which is governed by the referral-inducement boundary
clinical collaboration or care planning with those professionals, which is outside this business's scope

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: channel review shows referrals concentrating in sources the map ranked low, or a mapped contact leaves their role

pros.claim: A written landscape lets a one-person operation spend its limited relationship hours on sources whose rules actually permit sending business
pros.example: learning that the local hospital only distributes neutral lists while a senior-centre director actively recommends vendors, and sequencing effort accordingly

pros.claim: Recording what each source needs turns vendor calls into useful exchanges rather than requests for favours
pros.example: offering a home-care agency a short staff briefing on what to do when a client's device alarms, which the agency wanted anyway

cons.claim: Mapping is slow relational work whose payoff arrives long after the effort, which is punishing for a business needing revenue now
cons.example: three months of senior-centre and agency visits before the first referred installation appears

cons.claim: The map ages quickly because it is really a map of individuals, and staff in these roles turn over
cons.example: a carefully built discharge-planner relationship ending when that planner transfers to another unit

failure_modes: treating all sources as interchangeable and using one pitch across constrained and unconstrained channels
mapping organisations rather than the specific people inside them who actually make referrals
letting the map go stale so effort keeps flowing to a contact who left months ago
acceptance_tests: each mapped source carries its constraint note, its permissible help form, its stated need and a named current contact
the map distinguishes vendor-neutral sources from sources permitted to recommend, and the approach differs accordingly
revisit_triggers: a named contact leaves or changes role
a source organisation publishes or changes a vendor policy
a new senior-serving organisation opens in the service area

nodes.definition: Decide, in writing and before any handshake, what this business may give a referral source in return for business — because the answer is different for a healthcare-adjacent source than for a hardware shop, and getting it wrong contaminates the referrer as well as the operator. The obligation class covers anti-kickback and patient-inducement rules where the source touches healthcare, professional codes that bind social workers, nurses and care managers, employer policies at hospitals and agencies, and consumer-protection duties about undisclosed paid recommendations. None of the specifics are settled here: they vary by jurisdiction and source type and must be verified currently with counsel before any arrangement exists. What this node fixes is the operating posture — default to no payment of any kind for referrals from clinically-adjacent sources; keep reciprocity to things of no material value such as staff education, responsiveness and clear communication; disclose any commercial relationship that does exist to the family in plain words; and never make a gift contingent on volume. The test that survives every version of the rules is simple: could the referring family read the arrangement in full and still trust the recommendation?

included: the obligation classes governing referral compensation, each flagged for current jurisdictional verification
the default no-payment posture for clinically-adjacent sources and the permissible forms of reciprocity
the disclosure rule for any commercial relationship and the family-readability test
excluded: legal advice or a determination of what any specific statute permits, which requires counsel
employment compensation for the operator's own salespeople, which is a different arrangement entirely
family-to-family word of mouth after service, which belongs to the retention knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: counsel reports a change in the applicable inducement rules, or a source's employer policy on vendor relationships is published or revised

pros.claim: A default no-payment posture makes the boundary decidable in the moment without needing a legal opinion for every offer
pros.example: declining an agency manager's proposal of a fee per signed account and offering staff training and priority scheduling instead

pros.claim: Protecting the referrer from a compliance problem is itself a competitive advantage with professional sources
pros.example: a discharge planner continuing to include the operator on the neutral list because the operator never asked for anything that would compromise the planner

cons.claim: Competitors willing to pay for referrals will win volume in the short term from sources that accept payment
cons.example: losing a steady stream of agency referrals to a vendor offering a per-account bonus to schedulers

cons.claim: The rules genuinely vary, so a blanket refusal can forgo arrangements that are lawful and ordinary for non-clinical sources
cons.example: declining a straightforward disclosed advertising placement in a retirement community newsletter out of excessive caution

failure_modes: assuming a gift is fine because it is small, without checking the source's own employer policy or professional code
creating an informal reciprocal-referral understanding that neither side discloses to the families involved
acting on a rule remembered from another jurisdiction or from years ago
acceptance_tests: every referral arrangement in force is written down, disclosed to families, and free of volume-contingent value transfer
the file records that current jurisdictional rules were verified with counsel before any arrangement was entered
revisit_triggers: any source proposes payment, a gift or a revenue split
the business enters a new jurisdiction or adds a healthcare-adjacent source type
counsel or a source's employer flags an arrangement

nodes.definition: Work the discharge channel on its own terms: earn a place on a neutral resource list, be reliably available in the narrow discharge window, and never ask the planner to do anything that compromises their neutrality. Discharge planners and transition nurses meet families at the exact moment when going home alone becomes frightening, which makes them the highest-intent source in the landscape and also the most tightly constrained. They typically may hand a family a list of vendors but not steer to one; they are evaluated on readmission and on smooth transitions, not on vendor satisfaction; and they lose confidence in any vendor whose customer calls back to complain. The operator's usable levers are narrow and specific: a one-page factual capability sheet the planner can hand over, genuine same-week installation availability, a named human who answers the telephone, honest statements about what is not covered or supported, and an offer of short staff in-services that teach the unit's team what the device does when it alarms. Patient information never flows to the operator without the family's own consent; the family calls the operator, not the reverse.

included: earning and keeping a place on a vendor-neutral resource list
the discharge-window responsiveness commitments that make the listing useful
staff in-service education and the one-page factual capability sheet
excluded: receiving patient information without the individual's consent, which is prohibited
asking a planner to recommend this vendor over others, which compromises their neutrality
the installation appointment itself and its testing protocol, which belong to the device setup knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the institution revises its resource-list or transition policy, or discharge-sourced volume changes sharply after a staffing change on the unit

pros.claim: Discharge-sourced opportunities arrive with genuine need and a decision already forming, so effort converts far better than broad advertising
pros.example: a family calling from the hospital room on the day a Friday discharge is set, having been handed the resource list that morning

pros.claim: Responsiveness is a cheap, durable differentiator in this channel because most vendors cannot install inside the discharge window
pros.example: confirming a next-day installation while a competitor quotes the following week, without changing price at all

cons.claim: The channel demands operational readiness the business may not have, and one missed discharge-window promise can end the relationship
cons.example: failing a promised same-week installation during a staff illness and being quietly dropped from the list

cons.claim: Access is slow, gate-kept and personality-dependent, and neutrality rules cap how much volume it can ever produce
cons.example: months of polite contact before an in-service is permitted, and even then no recommendation is allowed

failure_modes: asking the planner for names and telephone numbers of patients being discharged
over-promising installation availability the business cannot staff, then missing the window
leaving a promotional sales flyer where a neutral factual capability sheet was required
acceptance_tests: the materials given to the unit are factual capability sheets with sourced claims, containing no superlatives and no pricing pressure
every discharge-sourced lead in the pipeline records that the family initiated contact, with no patient data received from the institution
revisit_triggers: the institution changes its vendor-list policy or its discharge process
a promised installation window is missed for any discharge-sourced family
the named planner contact changes role

nodes.definition: Build the home-care agency relationship around a genuinely shared interest rather than a referral favour: the agency's aides are in the house for a few hours a week and are acutely aware of the many hours they are not, and an alarm path covering those gaps reduces the incidents the agency will be blamed for. The workable arrangement has four parts. First, educate the agency's schedulers and aides on what the device does when it alarms and what it does not do, so nobody assumes it substitutes for a visit. Second, define the aide's boundary precisely — aides may notice, mention and hand over the operator's card, and may not sell, quote prices or promise capability, both because it is outside their role and because payment for their recommendations sits inside the inducement boundary. Third, agree how the operator handles an alarm involving a shared client, including whether the agency is a contact on the account, which is decided by the family and configured downstream. Fourth, keep the agency informed at the level the family consents to and no further. The relationship survives on reliability and on never putting an aide in an uncomfortable position with their client.

included: the shared-interest framing of the alliance and the education given to agency staff
the explicit boundary on what aides may and may not do about the product
consent-bounded information flow between operator and agency
excluded: configuring the agency into the emergency-contact tree, which is done in the device setup knowledge base
ongoing incident communication with the agency on live accounts, which belongs to the caregiver-relations knowledge base
any compensation to agency staff for referrals, which the inducement boundary forbids by default

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: agency staffing or ownership changes, or referred volume shifts after a briefing cycle, indicating whether the education is holding

pros.claim: Aides observe the actual risk signals no salesperson ever sees, so their unpaid, unpressured mention reaches the right households
pros.example: an aide noticing a client is now using furniture to move between rooms and leaving the operator's card with the family

pros.claim: Agency-referred families arrive pre-qualified and with a trusted third party already in the picture, which shortens and calms the sale
pros.example: a family that has already discussed the idea with the aide and only needs configuration and cost explained

cons.claim: The agency may see monitoring as competition for the same household budget rather than as a complement to its service
cons.example: an owner worrying that a monitored device gives a family the argument for cutting overnight hours

cons.claim: Aides are busy, turn over often and are not incentivised, so channel yield is unpredictable and education must be repeated
cons.example: a trained aide cohort largely replaced within a year, taking the product understanding with them

failure_modes: letting an aide quote prices or promise capability, which creates an unsubstantiated claim the operator must then honour or retract
positioning the device to the agency as a substitute for visit hours, which turns an ally into an opponent
sharing client details with the agency beyond what the family explicitly consented to
acceptance_tests: the written agency briefing states what aides may and may not say, and the agency has acknowledged it
no compensation of any kind flows to agency staff for referrals, and the information-sharing consent is recorded per household
revisit_triggers: agency staff turnover or a change of agency ownership
an aide is reported quoting prices or making capability promises
the agency raises the substitution concern about visit hours

nodes.definition: Earn standing invitations from senior centres, libraries, faith communities, retirement-community activity programmes and caregiver support groups by delivering genuinely useful education that is not a sales presentation, and accept that the sales benefit is indirect and delayed. The content that earns a second invitation is broader than the product: how emergency dispatch works locally, what to keep by the telephone, what a family should do when a parent has fallen and cannot be lifted, how to arrange a key-holder or lockbox so responders are not breaking a door, and where the honest limits of any alert device lie. The rules that keep the invitation open are strict — no pricing pressure in the room, no sign-up sheet framed as required, no fear imagery, no contact details taken without the person asking, and a clear statement at the start of who the speaker is and what they sell. Follow-up happens only with explicit permission recorded at the time. The channel's value is that it puts a named, unpressured human into a community long before the trigger event, which is the ethical alternative to arriving in a crisis.

included: the education content that earns repeat invitations and its explicit non-product portions
the in-room conduct rules including disclosure of who the speaker is and what they sell
consent-based follow-up recorded at the time of the event
excluded: collecting attendee contact details without a request, which is prohibited
device configuration and installation content, which belongs to the device setup knowledge base
support-group facilitation or counselling, which is outside this business's competence

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: venue invitations stop or accelerate, or attendee feedback indicates the talk is being received as a sales presentation

pros.claim: A useful, non-selling talk builds the pre-crisis familiarity that lets a family call a known name instead of the first advertisement they see
pros.example: an attendee's daughter telephoning eight months later, naming the talk her mother attended, on the day of a discharge

pros.claim: Venue gatekeepers become referral sources themselves once they trust that attendees are not pitched
pros.example: a centre director beginning to hand out the operator's card at the front desk after hosting two talks

cons.claim: The channel is slow and its attribution is poor, so it is the first thing cut when cash is tight and the last thing credited when it works
cons.example: a season of monthly talks with no directly traceable sale until much later

cons.claim: Speaking well is a distinct skill, and a weak or self-promoting talk can close a venue permanently
cons.example: a first talk that drifted into pricing and was not invited back

failure_modes: turning the talk into a product demonstration with a sign-up table at the exit
using a frightening anecdote or an unsourced statistic to hold attention
adding attendees to a call list without their explicit recorded permission
acceptance_tests: the talk outline devotes most of its content to non-product safety information and states the speaker's commercial interest at the start
every follow-up contact traces to a permission recorded at the event, with the record retained
revisit_triggers: a venue declines a repeat invitation or a gatekeeper raises a concern
the talk outline is changed or delivered by someone new
attendee feedback reports feeling sold to

nodes.definition: Decide deliberately how the offer is assembled, because the structure determines both what the customer risks and how the business earns. The components are few and each is a separate decision: the equipment and whether the customer buys it outright, leases it inside the subscription, or receives it as loaned property returnable on cancellation; a one-time activation or installation charge and whether it exists at all; the recurring monitoring subscription and its billing period; optional add-ons such as an additional pendant, a lockbox, a wall button, or a fall-detection capable device where that is a distinct product tier; and the term structure, which may be month-to-month, an annual prepayment at a stated discount, or a minimum-term commitment. This knowledge base takes a position on the ethical shape rather than the numbers: equipment loaned or leased rather than sold outright keeps the customer's downside small; month-to-month availability must exist even where prepayment is offered; and every add-on must be individually declinable with its own price stated. The specific figures are the operator's own, derived from their equipment cost, wholesale monitoring rate and local market, and no industry figure substitutes for that arithmetic.

included: the component decomposition of the offer and the ownership model for equipment
term structure options including a genuinely available month-to-month path
the rule that each add-on is separately priced and separately declinable
excluded: stating any specific price, wholesale rate or discount as an industry fact; all figures are the operator's own
which device model a household needs, which is determined by the home assessment in the device setup knowledge base
billing operations and payment collection on live accounts, which belong to the retention knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in equipment cost, wholesale monitoring rate, or equipment-return loss rate that alters which offer structure remains viable

pros.claim: Loaning or leasing the equipment inside the subscription keeps the customer's exposure to the cost of leaving small, which is both fair and a strong selling point
pros.example: a family who can end the service and return the base unit rather than being left holding equipment they bought outright

pros.claim: Separately priced, separately declinable add-ons stop the quiet inflation of a monthly bill nobody agreed to
pros.example: a lockbox and a second pendant each shown with their own charge, and the family taking only the lockbox

cons.claim: Loaned equipment ties up capital before any subscription revenue arrives and creates a recovery problem when accounts end
cons.example: several base units unreturned after cancellations, each a written-off asset

cons.claim: A simple offer that avoids commitments forgoes the cash and stability that prepayment and term contracts provide
cons.example: carrying the equipment and acquisition cost from a month-to-month account that ends before it has repaid anything

failure_modes: burying an activation charge or an equipment deposit where it is discovered on the first invoice
making the discounted annual prepayment the only practically available option
bundling fall detection into the base offer so a family pays for a capability tier they did not choose
acceptance_tests: the price sheet lists every component and add-on with its own charge, its billing frequency and whether it is one-time or recurring
a month-to-month path is available and quotable without penalty language, alongside any prepayment option
revisit_triggers: the wholesale monitoring rate or equipment cost changes
unreturned-equipment losses rise materially
a new product tier such as a mobile or fall-detection capable device is added

nodes.definition: State the complete cost of the first year, out loud and in writing, before asking the customer to decide anything. The all-in figure is the operator's own arithmetic across their own price sheet: every one-time charge, twelve months of the recurring subscription, every add-on the family has said yes to, shipping or installation if separate, and applicable tax, with the ongoing monthly figure stated separately so the family knows what continues after the first year. The disclosure rules that make this real are specific — the figure is given before the close rather than after agreement in principle; it is written on a single page the customer keeps; any charge that could ever appear later is named now, including equipment-damage or non-return charges, an address-change or reinstallation charge if one exists, and what happens to price at renewal; and if a promotional rate is used, the post-promotional figure is stated in the same breath as the promotional one. Automatic renewal and price-change notice duties are an obligation class to verify currently in the jurisdiction, but the practice here is deliberately stricter than any minimum: no charge should ever be a surprise on an invoice.

included: the all-in first-year figure and the separately stated ongoing monthly figure
the naming of every contingent charge before the decision is asked for
promotional-rate disclosure including the post-promotional figure, and the single page the customer keeps
excluded: publishing or asserting any specific price level as typical for the industry
invoice production, dunning and payment recovery on live accounts, which belong to the retention knowledge base
advice on whether a benefit programme or insurance will reimburse the cost, which is referred out

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a billing dispute or early cancellation cites a charge the customer says was never disclosed, or the price sheet changes

pros.claim: Full disclosure before the ask removes the invoice surprise that drives early cancellations and complaints in this industry
pros.example: naming the equipment non-return charge during the sales conversation so it never appears as a shock months later

pros.claim: The written one-page cost summary lets an absent sibling review the deal without a second sales conversation
pros.example: a son in another state reading the same page his mother has and agreeing without a follow-up call

cons.claim: A complete first-year figure sounds larger than a monthly figure and will lose price-shopping buyers to competitors quoting only the monthly rate
cons.example: a family comparing this all-in figure against a competitor's advertised monthly rate that omits activation and equipment

cons.claim: Disclosing every contingent charge lengthens the conversation and can overwhelm a listener already managing a family crisis
cons.example: a tired caregiver stopping the conversation partway through the charge list and asking to be called back

failure_modes: quoting only the monthly rate and letting activation, equipment and shipping appear later
presenting a promotional rate without stating what the price becomes afterward
leaving the total unwritten so the family has only a spoken recollection of what they agreed to
acceptance_tests: the customer holds a single written page showing every one-time charge, the recurring charge, the first-year total and the ongoing monthly figure
every contingent charge that can ever appear is named on that page, including non-return and post-promotional pricing
revisit_triggers: any price, fee or promotional structure changes
a customer disputes or questions a charge
an automatic-renewal or price-notice obligation changes in the jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Design the exit before designing the pitch, and treat easy cancellation as a feature of the product rather than a leak in the business. The terms that matter to this population are precise: how notice is given and to whom, whether it can be given by a family member or only the account holder, how prepaid time is refunded, what happens to the equipment and who pays return postage, whether any charge survives cancellation, and what happens when the wearer dies or moves into a care facility. The bereavement and higher-care paths deserve their own written clause because they are the most common ways these accounts end and the moments when a rigid term looks cruellest; the humane design cancels from notification, refunds unused prepaid time, and sends a prepaid return label rather than demanding a call from a grieving family. The commercial case is real rather than sentimental: families weigh the cost of being wrong when they buy, easy exit reduces that cost, referral sources notice how cancellations are handled, and a hard term buys a few extra months of billing at the price of the professional relationships the business runs on.

included: the written notice, proration, equipment-return and surviving-charge terms
the specific bereavement and move-to-higher-care clauses and who may give notice
the commercial argument that easy exit is a selling feature rather than a concession
excluded: executing cancellations, retention conversations and account closure on live accounts, which belong to the retention knowledge base
estate, probate or authority questions when an account holder dies, which are referred out
asserting any specific refund percentage or notice period as an industry standard

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: cancellation handling generates a complaint or a referrer's concern, or equipment-return losses change the viability of the current terms

pros.claim: Easy exit lowers the perceived risk of buying, which matters more than price to families who fear being trapped in another subscription
pros.example: a daughter agreeing to proceed once she reads that she can cancel by telephone and return the unit in a prepaid envelope

pros.claim: A written bereavement clause protects the referral relationships that a badly handled cancellation would destroy
pros.example: a home-care agency continuing to refer after seeing a family's account closed and refunded within days of a death, with no retention pitch

cons.claim: Frictionless cancellation shortens average account life and removes the term revenue that funds equipment and acquisition cost
cons.example: an account cancelling in its first months after the operator has already absorbed the equipment and installation cost

cons.claim: Generous refund and return terms create administrative work and equipment losses a very small operator absorbs personally
cons.example: prepaid return labels issued for units that are never actually posted back

failure_modes: requiring written notice by post, or requiring the account holder personally, when the account holder has died
keeping prepaid months on cancellation without saying so at the point of sale
routing cancellation requests into a retention script the family did not ask for
acceptance_tests: the cancellation terms fit on one plain-language page and name the notice method, the proration rule, the equipment-return path and any surviving charge
the bereavement and higher-care clauses exist in writing and require no argument from the family to invoke
revisit_triggers: a cancellation is handled in a way a family or referrer complains about
unreturned equipment losses rise materially
an automatic-renewal or cancellation-method obligation changes in the jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Understand how a single monitoring account repays what it cost to win, as a mechanism the operator fills with their own quoted numbers rather than as any figure taken from the industry. The mechanism has four moving parts. What goes out before revenue: the equipment unit at the operator's purchase cost, the installation visit at the operator's own labour and travel cost, and the acquisition cost attributable to the channel that produced the account. What comes in once: any activation charge and any margin on equipment sold outright. What comes in monthly: the subscription price less the wholesale per-account fee charged by the monitoring centre, less payment-processing and billing cost, less the amortised cost of servicing that account. And what governs the whole thing: how many months the account survives, because payback is reached only when accumulated monthly margin covers the up-front outlay. Three levers move the result and each is verifiable per deal — the wholesale rate the operator negotiates as account volume grows, the up-front cost of equipment and installation, and account longevity, which is bought with fit, assent and honest disclosure rather than with a term contract.

included: the four-part payback mechanism for a single account with the levers that move it
the requirement that the operator instantiate every term from their own quotes and invoices
the link between account longevity and payback, and therefore between honesty at sale and viability
excluded: any specific monetary figure, wholesale rate, margin percentage, payback duration or churn rate stated as fact
portfolio-level channel allocation, which is the channel-economics work unit
financial, tax or accounting advice on how to structure or finance the business

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a renegotiated monitoring contract, a change in equipment or processing cost, or observed account longevity that differs from the assumption used

pros.claim: A written mechanism makes the consequences of a short-lived account visible before it is sold, which disciplines the sale itself
pros.example: seeing that an account cancelling in its first months leaves the equipment and installation outlay unrecovered, and therefore refusing a sale where the wearer has not assented

pros.claim: Expressing economics as a mechanism keeps the model honest and portable when costs move, instead of freezing a number that quietly stops being true
pros.example: recomputing payback after renegotiating the wholesale monitoring rate at a higher account count, without rewriting the model

cons.claim: A mechanism gives no answer until the operator does the arithmetic with their own real quotes, which is work many small operators avoid
cons.example: an owner who has never separated the wholesale monitoring fee from the retail subscription price and cannot say what an account contributes

cons.claim: Per-account thinking can crowd out fixed costs, making the business look healthier than it is
cons.example: a positive per-account margin alongside a vehicle, telephone and insurance base the account count cannot yet carry

failure_modes: quoting an industry payback period or margin instead of computing from the operator's own invoices
ignoring the acquisition cost of the channel that produced the account when judging whether it was worth winning
treating equipment as free because it was already in the van
acceptance_tests: the model instantiates every term from a named internal document — an equipment invoice, the monitoring contract, a channel spend record — with no external figure asserted
the payback statement is expressed as a duration derived from those inputs, not as a claim about the industry
revisit_triggers: the monitoring contract, equipment cost or payment-processing cost changes
account volume crosses a tier that changes the wholesale rate
observed account longevity shifts materially in either direction

nodes.definition: Give families a comparison they can trust, across the dimensions that actually differ, while conceding openly the cases where a competitor is the better answer. The realistic alternative set is four-wide: nationally advertised monitored providers with call-centre sales and shipped self-installation; consumer electronics with emergency features such as a smartwatch or a mobile phone's emergency call function; unmonitored devices such as an auto-dialler that rings a relative directly; and doing nothing, which is what most households actually choose. The dimensions that genuinely separate them are who installs and verifies the equipment, whether anyone tests that a signal reaches the monitoring centre from that specific house, who answers when the button is pressed and what they are contracted to do, whether the wearer will actually wear it, what happens when the equipment fails, and the true all-in cost of each. Competitor claims are held to the same substantiation rule as the operator's own, which means no repeating a rumour about a rival's response times. The concessions must be explicit and rehearsed: a technology-comfortable, active person may be better served by a smartwatch, and a family who cannot afford a subscription is better served by an auto-dialler and a well-organised contact list than by a subscription that creates hardship.

included: the four-way alternative set including doing nothing, and the dimensions on which they genuinely differ
applying the substantiation rule to competitor claims as strictly as to the operator's own
the rehearsed concessions naming when a competitor or a cheaper alternative is the better fit
excluded: disparaging a named competitor with unsourced claims about their performance
technical device-capability evaluation and selection for a specific home, which belongs to the device setup knowledge base
advising a family on whether to spend money they do not have, which is personalized financial advice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a competitor's offering or a consumer-electronics capability changes materially, or a comparison claim is challenged and cannot be sourced

pros.claim: A comparison that concedes real cases converts scepticism into trust faster than any advantage claim, with exactly the family that has already been telephoned by three vendors
pros.example: telling an active seventy-year-old cyclist that a smartwatch with fall alerting may suit her better than a home base unit, and being called back for her mother

pros.claim: Comparing on installation, verification and who answers moves the conversation off price, where a local operator cannot win against national advertising
pros.example: explaining that the signal path from that specific back bedroom is measured at installation, which a shipped self-install box cannot offer

cons.claim: Conceding alternatives loses sales that a less scrupulous competitor would take, and the concession is invisible to everyone except the family who received it
cons.example: sending a household to a cheaper unmonitored option and receiving no revenue and no immediate referral

cons.claim: Maintaining an accurate, sourced comparison across changing competitor offerings is recurring work that decays fast
cons.example: a comparison sheet still describing a national provider's packaging that has since changed

failure_modes: repeating an unverified story about a competitor's answer times or hidden charges
comparing the operator's full-service price against a competitor's stripped monthly rate without matching the scope
omitting doing nothing from the alternative set, which is the choice most households actually make
acceptance_tests: every competitor claim used in a comparison names its source and its date, and no claim about a competitor is asserted without one
the comparison material contains at least two written cases in which an alternative is conceded to be the better fit
revisit_triggers: a competitor changes packaging, pricing structure or capability
a new consumer-electronics feature becomes a realistic substitute
a family reports being told something about a competitor that turned out to be untrue

nodes.definition: Screen every opportunity against a written list of conditions under which this business does not sell, and make declining a normal, recorded outcome rather than a failure. The disqualifying conditions are concrete: no viable signal path at the address for any product carried, which is screened by asking about the household's telephone and mobile-signal situation before an installation is promised and confirmed properly at the home assessment; a wearer who does not assent after the objections have been genuinely heard; a household whose stated situation indicates a level of need beyond what an alarm button addresses, such as someone who cannot press a button or cannot be left alone at all; a household for whom the subscription would compete with essentials; and a caller seeking a clinical answer rather than a product. Each condition has a scripted decline, an alternative to offer — a referral to the public ageing-services agency class, a suggestion to speak with the discharge team or clinician, an unmonitored option, or simply an invitation to call back later — and a short written record naming the condition, the alternative and who was told. The decline record is what makes the rule auditable and what stops it eroding in a slow month.

included: the enumerated disqualifying conditions screened before a sale is progressed
the scripted decline, the alternative offered, and the written decline record
the pre-sale connectivity screening question that precedes any installation promise
excluded: the on-site range, connectivity and mounting assessment that definitively confirms feasibility, which belongs to the device setup knowledge base
judging a person's care needs or capacity, which is referred to a clinician or care professional
cancelling or downgrading an existing live account, which belongs to the retention knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: installations failing their end-to-end signal test on accounts that passed pre-sale screening, or a new product class changing what is feasible

pros.claim: A written decline list prevents the sale that becomes a refund, a complaint and a lost referral source two months later
pros.example: declining a household with no usable mobile signal and no landline instead of installing equipment that will fail its own signal test

pros.claim: Declining visibly and offering a genuine alternative is one of the strongest trust signals a professional referrer ever receives
pros.example: a discharge planner learning the operator turned away a patient and pointed the family to the ageing-services agency instead

cons.claim: Every decline is revenue refused, and in a thin month the list is exactly what a struggling operator is tempted to reinterpret
cons.example: arguing that a marginal signal situation is probably fine because the month's numbers are short

cons.claim: Screening on a caller's description can decline a household that would in fact have worked, since only the home assessment is definitive
cons.example: turning away a family who described their coverage as poor when a different carrier or a mobile unit would have served them

failure_modes: selling first and discovering at installation that no signal path exists, leaving the family to be unwound
treating the wearer's refusal as an objection to overcome rather than a decline condition
declining without offering any alternative, which leaves a household with a real need and nowhere to go
acceptance_tests: each disqualifying condition has a scripted decline and a named alternative destination in the written procedure
declines are recorded with the condition, the alternative offered and the date, and the record is reviewable
revisit_triggers: a product with different connectivity is added that changes what is feasible
an installation fails its signal test on an account that passed pre-sale screening
the decline rate moves sharply in either direction

nodes.definition: Run the sales conversation in a fixed order that puts every disclosure ahead of every ask, so that honesty is structural rather than dependent on the salesperson's mood.
